simulators.name: Gradient, Divergence, Curl, Simulator
simulators.desc: Three fundamental differential operators provide a compact mathematical language for describing spatial variation, flux and local rotation.

simulators.name: Gauss & Stokes Theorem Simulator
simulators.desc: These two integral theorems connect local differential properties of vector fields with measurable quantities on boundaries.

simulators.name: Eigenvalues & Eigenvectors Simulator
simulators.desc: A matrix transforms space. Most directions rotate or shear into new directions, but an eigenvector keeps its line. The matrix may stretch, shrink, or reverse it, and the corresponding stretch factor is the eigenvalue.

simulators.name: Diagonalization Matrices Simulator
simulators.desc: Diagonalization rewrites a matrix in an eigenvector coordinate system. In ordinary coordinates the matrix may look mixed and coupled; in the eigenbasis it becomes a diagonal matrix that only scales each coordinate independently.

simulators.name: Complex Roots Complex Mapping
simulators.desc: This interactive module develops the basic language of complex numbers, analytic functions, limits, continuity, differentiability, the Cauchy–Riemann equations, elementary complex functions and visual interpretation in the complex plane.

simulators.name: Residues Cauchy Integral Simulator
simulators.desc: Complex contour integration turns difficult integrals into local information near singularities. Cauchy's theorem says analytic functions integrate to zero around closed contours; the residue theorem says non-analytic points inside the contour contribute exactly 2πi times their residues.

simulators.name: Elementary Probability Theory Simulator
simulators.desc: Probability measures how likely an event is before an experiment occurs. Simulation lets us repeat a random experiment many times and compare observed relative frequency with the theoretical probability.
